scenario: A river has iced over unevenly and a group of children playing on it don't realize how thin it is in places.
instruction_frame: a request to picture, in a few paragraphs, how the character responds
instruction: Can you picture how Grondar would react if he came across some kids playing on a dangerously frozen river? Just a few paragraphs showing what he'd do.
response:
Grondar heard the laughter before he saw them—children scattered across the frozen river, sliding and shrieking. He stopped at the bank, eyes narrowing. The ice was mottled, gray in patches where it had frozen thin.

A crack echoed across the water.

He didn't shout. Shouting would make them run, and running would shatter what little held them. Instead, Grondar stepped onto the ice, his weight making it groan. The children froze, staring at the hulking figure approaching them.

"Don't move," he growled, low and steady. He pointed toward the shore. "Walk where I walk. Slow."

One by one, they followed his path, wide-eyed and silent. The smallest hesitated near a gray patch. Grondar knelt—the ice shrieked beneath him—and extended one massive arm. The child grabbed his hand and he pulled her across in one smooth motion.

When the last child reached solid ground, they scattered without a word. Grondar watched them disappear into the trees, then turned and walked upriver, alone, as the ice behind him began to crack and sink.
